value.rationale: The first failure of a natural information-theoretic upper bound for all two-chain merge comparisons occurs uniquely at seven total elements and profile (3,4). Its root-split obstruction identifies a structural failure of balanced adaptive shattering, and a complete decision tree plus sharp smaller-case survey proves minimality. This is a meaningful first natural cutoff beyond an already known two-row theory; earlier two-row results are not rebranded as new.
